body:
Proposal from the Axiomancer integration work. Written for the daily scout's builder agent to consume and implement — each section is an independent contract; land them in order.

## Context

Axiomancer's design skills (`brainstorm-mechanics`, `mechanics-expert`) now sync this repo into a gitignored `kb/` and grep it for prior art, citing `kb:<game-slug>/<doc> (src-NNN)`. Coverage requests arrive in `WISHLIST.md` (seeded on `main`; first entry is live). The changes below make retrieval surgical as the corpus grows daily, and give the corpus a maintenance loop.

## 1. Spec bump: OKF 0.2 frontmatter

Add two fields to the required frontmatter in `OKF_SPEC.md`; the scout emits them on every new doc:

```yaml
mechanics: []        # controlled slugs, e.g. [deck-building, push-your-luck, co-op-ai, hand-management]
better_if_labels: [] # only on type: better_if / reception docs — labels from the existing better-if taxonomy
```

Rules:
- `mechanics` is a controlled vocabulary. Start from BGG mechanism names, kebab-cased; keep a canonical list in `OKF_SPEC.md` and extend it there first (never invent per-doc synonyms — `deckbuilding` vs `deck-building` splits retrieval).
- `better_if_labels` reuses the taxonomy already in the spec (onboarding, downtime, runaway-leader, ...), kebab-cased, verbatim.
- Bump `okf_version: 0.2`. Backfill the five existing games in one pass.

**Why:** this is the metadata firewall. Agents currently must read doc bodies to learn what a game is about; with tags they grep frontmatter and only open the two docs that matter.

## 2. Generated corpus index: `KnowledgeBase/BoardGames/INDEX.okf.md`

One generated file, regenerated at the end of every scout run (and by the librarian). One line per game:

```md
| slug | title | year | weight | mechanics | top better-if labels | status | docs |
```

Plus a second table: mechanics slug → game slugs (the inverted index). Keep it under a few hundred lines even at 100 games — it is the first (often only) file an agent reads. `index.html` stays the human dashboard; this is its machine twin.

## 3. Patterns layer: `KnowledgeBase/BoardGames/patterns/`

Cross-game synthesis docs keyed to the better-if taxonomy and major mechanics: `patterns/runaway-leader.okf.md`, `patterns/push-your-luck.okf.md`, etc. Each is `type: pattern` (new enum value), aggregates claims across games with back-references (`game-slug (src-NNN)`), and ends with a `Design implications for SomberSoft` section synthesizing the cross-game view.

Cadence: weekly, not per-run — a synthesis pass that reads what changed since the last pass and updates only affected pattern docs. Recommended host: **this repo's own GitHub Actions workflow** (weekly cron) running Claude with a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` repo secret — patterns are a derived artifact *of* this corpus and should version and run with it, not with any consumer repo. The runner pattern in Axiomancer's `.github/workflows/_claude-skill.yml` can be copied nearly verbatim (minus the Node/npm and enforcement steps).

## 4. Librarian gate (two parts)

**4a. Mechanical validator (plain script, every push):** a small Node script + workflow that checks every `*.okf.md`: required frontmatter fields present, enum values legal (`type`, `confidence`, `status`, `provenance`), `mechanics`/`better_if_labels` drawn from the controlled vocabularies, every `Source: src-NNN` referenced by a claim exists in that doc's `sources` block, and INDEX freshness (regenerate and diff — fail if stale). This needs no model and no tokens; it is the corpus's type-checker.

**4b. Weekly librarian pass (Claude, same workflow slot as §3 or its own):** drain `status: needs_followup` — retry failed extractions with better tooling (e.g. Mage Knight's official PDFs, whose facts currently rest on search snippets, honestly labeled), upgrade claim confidence where verification succeeds, flip status to `verified`, merge/flag near-duplicate docs, and check off completed `WISHLIST.md` entries.

## 5. Scout selection: consume `WISHLIST.md`

Selection doctrine amendment: before free selection, take the topmost unchecked `WISHLIST.md` entry; check it off in the same run that covers it (link the new game dir). Free-choice selection applies only when the wishlist is empty. This turns daily growth from "whatever the scout felt like" into demand-driven coverage.

## 6. Failed-source policy (decision requested → recommendation)

Question raised: should the scout stash the *failed source documents themselves* (e.g. unparseable PDFs) so the librarian can handle them?

**Recommendation: no raw stashing.** Storing fetched rulebook PDFs/HTML in the repo conflicts with the existing copyright doctrine ("do not mirror whole copyrighted rulebooks") and bloats a repo that consumers shallow-clone. Instead, make failures *structured and retryable*: a per-game `followups.okf.md` (or a `followups:` frontmatter block in `scout-report.okf.md`) with, per failure: source id + exact URL, what failed (TLS, timeout, PDF extraction), what was used as fallback, and what a retry needs (browser fetch, PDF tooling). The librarian (§4b) consumes exactly this. The scout already writes honest failure notes in prose — this just makes them machine-consumable.

## Suggested landing order

1. §1 + backfill (unblocks everything)
2. §2 index generation (immediate retrieval win)
3. §4a validator (locks the format before the corpus grows further)
4. §5 wishlist consumption (the demand loop is already live on the producer side)
5. §3 patterns + §4b librarian (needs the token secret added to this repo)
